summary: At segment 0 step 37, selecting the blessed enchant-weapon scroll reaches read.c:seffect_enchant_weapon. C draws rnd(3)=2 at read.c:1670; JavaScript routes blessed scrolls to note_unported and skips the effect, so the aligned rn2(12)=1 is subsequent stream drift. Port the complete seffect_enchant_weapon function and its consumed-result wield.c:chwepon callee; chwepon’s integer result controls whether the scroll is consumed. Preserve the existing doread/seffects caller chain and source-ordered cap_spe behavior.

source.branch: For the recorded path, doread selects a blessed SCR_ENCHANT_WEAPON with a wielded non-eroded quarterstaff while the hero is not confused. seffect_enchant_weapon reaches its blessed branch; because the weapon is below +9, C computes s with rnd(3) (the recorded draw) and passes the result to chwepon(), then caps the weapon enchantment. The full function also includes cursed, confused erosion-proofing, no-weapon, and high-enchantment branches.
callers: C: cmd.c command table at 1817 dispatches the read command to read.c:doread() (330); doread() calls seffects() at 635, whose SCR_ENCHANT_WEAPON arm at 2233-2234 calls seffect_enchant_weapon() at 1627-1676. The function consumes chwepon()’s result at 1672 to null the scroll pointer before seffects() returns the use-up decision to doread().

JavaScript: js/cmd.js read handler (3410-3415) calls js/read.js:doread(); js/read.js:seffects() handles SCR_ENCHANT_WEAPON at 1582-1595, but its guard rejects blessed scrolls into note_unported. The existing js/read.js:seffect_enchant_weapon() at 1672-1692 is restricted to ordinary scrolls and calls js/wield.js:chwepon() with hard-coded amount 1.
dependencies: wield.c:chwepon() (918-1048) is the required return-valued dependency: read.c consumes its int result and treats zero as strange_feeling() having consumed the scroll. The current JS chwepon() at js/wield.js:319-353 only supports amount=1 on an ordinary positive branch; it refuses the blessed amount selected here and does not propagate a false result to seffects(). This is the only C chwepon() call site (read.c:1672).

objnam.c:erosion_matters() (1195-1215) returns a boolean consumed by the confused branch at read.c:1640. It is pure by source inspection and its existing JS counterpart is obj.js:erosionMatters() at 1474-1480; verify that helper/test/source-file placement when completing the whole read.c function.
read.c:cap_spe() (80-86) is a void state clamp called at read.c:1675. js/read.js currently mirrors the absolute SPE_LIM clamp inline after chwepon(); preserve that source order and bound.

The complete chwepon() body also consumes existing helper or macro results including is_weptool, will_weld, has_oname, restrict_name, u_wield_art/is_art, weight, and is_elven_weapon. Existing JS counterparts cover the helpers/macros except is_elven_weapon, which can be expressed from obj.h:360-363 inside the wield.c port; its void side-effect callees must follow the source-gap rule.

evidence: The saved A25 queue and evaluation challenges/evaluations/20260927111723-v8.json at 358dd6ad1294374a96a704a7f5a9b46c0ddc4a47 still show 1 remaining screen over 38 steps: 37/38 screens, 2757/2758 RNG entries, and 37/38 cursors match. At segment 0 step 37 (key o), the first RNG mismatch is index 2757: C rnd(3)=2 at seffect_enchant_weapon(read.c:1670), JS rn2(12)=1; screen index 37 differs at row 0 column 38, C '-' versus JS space, with cursors C [46,0,1] and JS [29,14,1].

The immutable C recording challenges/cases/v8/read-blessed-enchant-weapon.session.json records step 37 input o with rn2(19)=4 @ exercise(attrib.c:509), then rnd(3)=2 @ seffect_enchant_weapon(read.c:1670), and the screen begins “As you read the scroll, it disappears.--More--”. Its independently selected recipe is challenges/cases/v8/read-blessed-enchant-weapon.recipe.session.json (seed 83015418, Wizard, wished blessed scroll, then read).

Upstream read.c:1627-1676 shows the full effect. At 1667-1671, a blessed scroll with a wielded weapon below +9 selects rnd(3 - uwep->spe / 3); the recorded rnd(3) confirms this branch. At 1672, the chwepon() result controls *sobjp; at 1675, cap_spe() runs afterward.

Upstream read.c:2193-2234 dispatches SCR_ENCHANT_WEAPON to seffect_enchant_weapon(); read.c:doread() consumes seffects()’s result at 635-645. The missing JavaScript source branch is visible in js/read.js:1582-1595; the current effect at 1672-1692 explicitly rejects blessed scrolls. The C call graph has one chwepon() site, at read.c:1672.

Upstream wield.c:918-1048 defines the complete chwepon() function, including the integer return branches. The JavaScript implementation at js/wield.js:319-353 is only the ordinary amount=1 branch, confirming that the effect cannot be completed safely by changing only the blessed RNG formula.

The additional consumed helper objnam.c:erosion_matters() is pure: its source at 1195-1215 only inspects object class and calls is_weptool(). Its existing JS behavior is obj.js:1474-1480. The void cap_spe() helper’s absolute clamp is currently mirrored inline in js/read.js.
